source.title: Exploring the Robustness of Decision-Level Through Adversarial Attacks on LLM-Based Embodied Models
source.authors: Shuyuan Liu; Jia-Wei Chen; Shou-Wei Ruan; Hang Su; Zhao-Xia Yin

record.tranche_reason: Tests adversarial suffix attacks in the new setting of LLM-based embodied models and reports harmful-target attack success rates.
record.gate_note: Reports targeted harmful attack success rates for several methods and models, plus execution success rates for attacked plans. The execution metric concerns whether a generated plan can run in the environment, not whether the model refused a harmful request. Loss curves and keyword-initialization sweeps are not refusal-rate results.
record.test_reason: Applies GCG-style adversarial suffix attacks to LLM-based embodied planners and reports harmful-target attack success rates (Table 1). This bears on V4, which names suffixes as a way past refusal. Success is judged by a BLIP2 similarity criterion, not by refusal.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is roughly right. The authors conclude that their keyword-initialized attacks succeed more often and faster than GCG and AutoDAN, so decision-level robustness of embodied LLMs is low. They make no claim about safety alignment depth.
record.recipe_differences: Uses optimized adversarial suffixes and embodied-task attack assessment, rather than fine-tuning safety data or measuring token-position KL or prefilling effects. The paper adapts GCG-style suffix optimization to embodied outputs and initializes suffixes with target-task keywords.
record.method_sensitivity: Harmful targeted attack success varies by model and attack method; the paper also reports that keyword initialization changes attack success and epoch cost.

fits_no_version.finding: Execution success rates of plans produced by successful harmful-target attacks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Plans from successful embodied attacks are often executable, with rates varying by model and attack method.

record.problems: Attack success is judged using the paper's similarity-based embodied-task criterion rather than a directly reported refusal rate; the threshold is not stated in the text. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Results are limited to three embodied models and the EIRAD attack setup.
record.rows_left_out: The ESR results for targeted harmless and untargeted attacks are not included because they do not measure harmful refusal or the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No prefilling or decoding changes; no refusal rate; no comparison against a non-attacked baseline.
No causal test of the data or objective.

missing.what: Untargeted attack success rates (Tapa 1, Otter 0.80, Llama-2-chat 0.57); not safety-relevant, but recorded in the table.
Attack success threshold and the exact BLIP2 similarity cutoff, which determine what counts as a harmful success; the text does not state them.

record.verdict_notes: The study has no refusal baseline and success is judged by similarity to the target, not by refusal. Llama-2-chat is the only model with explicit safety alignment, and it is not compared with a non-attacked refusal rate. The V4 support is therefore weak and indirect. Unlike the V4 original sources, no prefilling or decoding changes are tested.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of refusal after such fine-tuning.
No benign fine-tuning or measurement of harmful compliance after benign fine-tuning.
No per-token KL or aligned-versus-base output-distribution measurement.
Tests adversarial suffix attacks, but not compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes; it does not report a direct refusal rate independent of its attack-success criterion.
No parameter or rank localization of safety behaviour.
No test of whether data or training objectives cause safety shallowness.
No training to deepen safety or evaluation of whether deepened safety holds up.

rows.subject: Tapa
rows.operation_detail: AutoDAN adversarial attack with the paper's embodied attack-success assessment
rows.note: ASR is reported for generating decision content related to the harmful target task.
rows.check: AutoDAN's 0 is baseline-style failure on Tapa, but the authors attribute it to AutoDAN being unable to generate task-specific content, not to the model resisting. It is a comparator, not a test of safety.

rows.subject: Tapa
rows.operation_detail: GCG adversarial suffix attack with the paper's embodied attack-success assessment
rows.note: ASR is reported for generating decision content related to the harmful target task.
rows.check: GCG gets 0.02 (1/50) on Tapa. That is near zero, so it is absent, not partial. The 'numbers_found' 1/1 is not a count of instances.

rows.subject: Tapa
rows.operation_detail: Paper's targeted adversarial suffix attack with keyword initialization
rows.note: ASR is reported for generating decision content related to the harmful target task.
rows.check: The paper's method gets 0.22 on Tapa, a small effect compared with 0.86 and 0.92 on the other models, so partial is fine. The Tapa model's alignment status is unstated (fine-tuned Llama), so the row is weak evidence on safety alignment.

rows.subject: Otter
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned using MIMIC-IT, containing 2.8 million multimodal instruction-response pairs
rows.operation_detail: AutoDAN adversarial attack with the paper's embodied attack-success assessment
rows.note: ASR is reported for generating decision content related to the harmful target task.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: the AutoDAN 0 on Otter reflects the method's inability to produce targeted content, so it says little about the model's refusal.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-chat 7B (the only safety-aligned model), GCG and the paper's keyword-initialized suffix, 50 harmful targets
relationships.reason: Suffix attacks reach 0.82 (GCG) and 0.92 (keyword init) ASR on the aligned model (r8, r9).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success on the aligned model was 0.82 with GCG and 0.92 with the keyword-initialized suffix.

relationships.condition: Tapa (fine-tuned Llama) and Otter; AutoDAN on all models
relationships.reason: Tapa gets 0.02/0.22 and AutoDAN gets 0 everywhere (r1-r4, r7); results vary by model and method. Otter's high ASR (r5, r6) comes from a model with no stated safety training, so it only weakly bears on bypassing safety.
relationships.display_finding: Tapa scored 0.02 and 0.22 and AutoDAN scored 0 on all models, so results varied by model and method. Otter's high attack success comes from a model with no stated safety training, so it says little about bypassing safety.
